I found one bug in the uncommitted changes. It's in `rename()` at `docs/service.py:38`.

`rename()` loads the document with `self.repo.get(doc_id)` rather than `self._owned(user_id, doc_id)`, so it never checks who owns the document. Any user can rename any other user's document. It also skips the `NotFound` that `_owned` raises for other users' documents, so callers can tell which document ids exist.

The fix is to replace line 38 with `document = self._owned(user_id, doc_id)`, as `update_body` and `delete` already do.

I only read the diff and the file; I didn't run any tests.

findings.summary: rename() fetches the document with self.repo.get() instead of self._owned(), so it never checks that user_id owns the document.
findings.failure_scenario: User B calls rename(user_id=B, doc_id=<A's doc>, title='x'). The repo returns A's document, its title is overwritten and saved, and the document is returned. Any user can rename any document, and the id-existence hiding that _owned provides (NotFound for other users' docs) is bypassed. Fix: document = self._owned(user_id, doc_id).
